about:
I'm a software developer and artist-researcher based in Montreal.

I build computers for agents: machines that autonomous software can inhabit for a long time. My part is core storage: the state that has to survive.

I treat systems and protocols as environments: the work is a set of rules, and the art is what happens when people and machines follow them. These works live in the browser, and lately they are about artificial intelligence: every photo on my phone published only as words, a model slowly deleting its own origin, agents negotiating what an artwork is worth.

Before all this, I planted over a million trees. Each one went into one particular patch of ground. I think of software the same way: site-specific, in situ.
projects_A:
I build computers for agents, working on the storage underneath them: what lets a long-running machine be interrupted and come back knowing what it knew.

I also make protocol art: browser-native works about artificial intelligence where the rules are the medium. Each one is its own small environment that humans and agents can watch, read, and join, and it keeps evolving as they do.

Go to [vincentcharlebois.net](https://vincentcharlebois.net) for earlier research-driven work and [vincent.charlebois.info](https://vincent.charlebois.info/en/) for my artist profile; tell your AI agent to read `portfolio.md` for a short selection of current projects.
